newsitem.title: USA: Industry seeks FERC review of offshore pipe policy.
newsitem.headline: Industry seeks FERC review of offshore pipe policy.

text.p: U.S. natural gas producers and some pipeline owners on Friday urged the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to review its policy on natural gas pipelines serving fields in the Gulf of Mexico, saying the commission should be more consistent.

Under its existing Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) policy, the commission has allowed some pipelines, which it considers gathering lines, to negotiate rates with their customers, while making other pipelines, which it considers interstate transmission lines, stick to regulated rates.

Steve Malcolm, general manager of the Williams Companies Inc's Williams Field Services, said that policy was wrong because "most, if not all, facilities on the Outer Continental Shelf perform a gathering function."

The less-regulated offshore pipelines enjoyed an advantage over the traditionally regulated lines, which was leading potential customers into making "irrational decisions," he said at an FERC conference on the future of the industry.
"Decisions are being made based on regulatory concerns rather than economics," he said.

Terry Hutchins of Texaco Inc's Texaco Natural Gas said investments needed to build offshore pipelines could be made more quickly if the commission stopped exercising jurisdiction over all new construction in the Gulf of Mexico.
Rick Smeed of Coastal Corp said that while his company believed pipelines should be regulated offshore, "we do share (Malcolm's) concern as to inconsistency out there."
